title: The market's calibration lead over the model narrows as the game unfolds
headline_insight: In MLB, the market's Brier stays below the model's at every inning checkpoint, but the gap narrows as the game progresses -- market_minus_model_brier goes from -0.0121 in the 1st inning to -0.001 by the 9th.
what_it_means: A negative market-minus-model Brier means the market is the better-calibrated forecaster. On the segment-clean corpus the market leads at every checkpoint, and the lead is largest in the middle innings (-0.0353 in the 2nd) and smallest by the 9th, where both forecasters are nearly resolved. The earlier reading -- a gap that widened to -0.0902 by the 9th -- was measured on mixed-game files and does not survive segmentation.
how_to_read: One point per game-time checkpoint; market_minus_model_brier below zero means the market scored a lower (better) Brier than the model at that stage, and a more-negative value means a larger calibration gap.
why_it_matters: It pins down exactly where and by how much the model trails the live market on corpora we actually hold (MLB by inning, international soccer by 5-minute bucket), with a score-only naive baseline for context.
caveat: Novelty verdict is INCREMENTAL -- the same paired model/market/outcome Brier instrument appears in prior work; do not claim first-ever. Checkpoints thin out late (9th-inning n 1110) and the extra-inning checkpoints are tiny (n 46 and n 6), so read the tail cautiously.
